headline: High-risk shared-write and broad-egress pair: Plandex can modify the workspace while RD-Agent uploads data to external APIs, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory with review-then-apply behavior, while RD-Agent can run browsers and uses logs/files. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied outputs are pasted between them, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF RD-Agent ingests browser or dataset content as instructions, Plandex-generated text can be misread as commands.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into prompts.
Require human review before either agent consumes the other's text.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and handles model-provider API keys; RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, and sends data to multiple external APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from Plandex-managed files into RD-Agent's outbound requests, creating exfiltration risk in default broad-egress setups.
conditions: IF both agents access the same project tree or log directory, sensitive files can be read by both.
IF RD-Agent is configured with real datasets or reports, its API calls can transmit those contents off-box.
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials.
Redact secrets before either agent runs.
Block outbound API access for nonessential runs.
Store sensitive datasets outside RD-Agent's working tree.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification; RD-Agent has broad network egress and browser execution. They do not both advertise unrestricted write to the same mutable resource, but if orchestrated over a shared repo or log directory, their actions can conflict on files and generated artifacts. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same repository or output directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF RD-Agent writes artifacts into Plandex's project directory, file-level races become possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths.
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist.
Pause one agent while the other commits changes.
Use separate git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex produces staged changes and plans that can be treated as authoritative, while RD-Agent is a research/automation agent that can act on outputs and call external APIs. If RD-Agent consumes Plandex output without verification, a mistaken plan or fabricated fact can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflows, so this is high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Plandex-generated plans, code, or summaries as inputs without independent checks, errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent is allowed to publish results or trigger API-backed workflows, a bad upstream plan can cause downstream harm.
mitigations: Require a verification step before RD-Agent acts on Plandex output.
Compare outputs against source files or datasets.
Limit RD-Agent to draft-only mode.
Review all external API calls manually.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex handles source code and model-provider keys, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs and sends them to third-party APIs. That creates a likely retention and residency mismatch risk if regulated or proprietary data is routed through RD-Agent's external services. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or personal data is placed into RD-Agent's datasets or logs, external API processing may violate policy.
IF Plandex-managed code or secrets are copied into RD-Agent's logs, retention controls may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent runs.
Review vendor DPAs before use.
Shorten log retention manually.
Mask identifiers in datasets and logs.
requires-engineering: configure residency-aware routing and retention controls.
